1173.subject: Chemistry
1173.text: Which of the following is always feasible?
options: $\Delta H$ (-ve), $T \Delta S$ (+ve) and $\Delta H < T \Delta S$
1173.sol:
Feasibility of reaction is determined by free energy change value $(\Delta G) . \Delta G$ is given by Gibbs - Helmholtz equation :

\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S

Reaction is feasible if $\Delta G$ value is negative. Therefore, if $\Delta H$ is negative and $T \Delta S$ is positive then the $\Delta G$ will always be feasible.

2065.text: Which of the following are uricotelic animals?
2065.sol: Uricotelic animals (living in dry conditions) are those animals which excrete uric acid as their excretory product e.g. lizard and crow. These animals conserve water in their bodies and synthesize crystals of uric acids from ammonia. These crystals can be retained in the body (in solid form) for a considerable time before being discharged from the body.

The human retina contains 6-7 million cones which function best in bright light and are essential for active vision (receiving a sharp accurate image). 3813.subject: Chemistry
3813.text: Which hormone tends to increase the blood glucose level in human?
3813.sol:
Hormones have several functions in the body. They help to maintain the balance of biological activities in the body.

The role of insulin in keeping the blood glucose level within the narrow limit is an example of this function. Insulin is released in response to the rapid rise in blood glucose level. On the other hand hormone glucagon tends to increase the glucose level in the blood. The two hormones together regulate the glucose level in the blood.

Epinephrine and norepinephrine mediate responses to external stimuli.

Estrogen or oestrogen is a category of sex hormone responsible for the development and regulation of the female reproductive system and secondary sex characteristics.

In terms of chemical nature, some of these are steroids, e.g., estrogens and androgens; some are poly peptides for example insulin and endorphins and some others are amino acid derivatives such as epinephrine and norepinephrine

4186.subject: Chemistry
4186.text: Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity for nucleophilic addition reaction
4186.sol:
Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition reactions due to steric and electronic reasons. Sterically, the presence of two relatively large substituents in ketones hinders the approach of nucleophile to carbonyl carbon than in aldehydes having only one such substituent. Electronically, aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because two alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more effectively than in former.

Benzophenone being a ketone is the least reactive towards nucleophilic addition. All others are aldehydes. Among them, p-tolualdehyde is less reactive than benzaldehyde because CH_{3}& group present at the para position w.r.t.& -CHO group will increase the electron density on the carbonyl carbon atom due to hyper conjugation effect. As a result, the nucleophile attack occurs to lesser extent as compared to benzaldehyde.

In p-nitrobenzaldehyde, the nitro group has an opposing effect. It is electron withdrawing in nature due to -I effect as well as -R effect. The electron density on the carbonyl carbon atom decreases and this favours the nucleophile attack.

Hence, the correct order of reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution reaction is Benzophenone

5956.text: The boiling point of water at $1 \mathrm{ atm}$ is $100^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. Which among the following is true for vaporisation of water at $75^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ ?
5956.sol:
According to standard Gibbs free energy equation
i.e.,

\begin{aligned}$ \Delta$ G^{{}^{\circ}}=$\Delta H^{{}^{\circ}}-T $\Delta$ S^{{}^{\circ}} \\
 $\Delta$ G^{{}^{\circ}}=-T $\Delta$ S^{{}^{\circ}} \\
 $\Delta$ G^{{}^{\circ}} \propto-T
\end{aligned}

It means $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}$ is inversely proportional to temperature due to negative sign present in Gibbs free energy equation.
Hence, lesser the temperature i.e., $75^{{}^{\circ}} $\mathrm{C}$, greater the value of $\Delta^{{}^{\circ}} G_{\text{vap }}   \left(\Delta G_{\text{vap }$}$^0 > 0\right)$.
At $100^{{}^{\circ}}  \mathrm{C}, \Delta G_{\text{vap }}^0$value is lesser than that at temperature 75^{{}^{\circ}}  $\mathrm{C}$.\therefore Vaporisation$ of $water at 75^{{}^{\circ}}$\mathrm{C}$has \Delta G_{$\text{vap }}^{{}^{\circ}} > 0$.

Given quadratic equation is x²-2 x+4=0 whose roots are $\alpha$ and $\beta$. \therefore \quad $\alpha+\beta=2 \text{$ and $} \alpha \beta=4 Now, \begin{aligned}& \alpha^9+\beta^9=\left(\alpha^3\right)^3+\left(\beta^3\right)^3 \\

= & (\alpha+\beta) \left(\alpha^2-\alpha \beta+\beta^2\right)\left[\left(\alpha^2\right)^3+\left(\beta^2\right)^3-\alpha^3 \beta^3\right] \\
= & (\alpha+\beta) \left[(\alpha+\beta)^2-3 \alpha \beta\right]\\
& \quad\left[ \left(\a alpha^2+\beta^2\right) \left(\a alpha^4+\b beta^4-\alpha^2 \beta^2\right)-\alpha^3 \beta^3\right]\\
= & (\alpha+\beta) \left[(\alpha+\beta)^2-3 \alpha \beta\right]\left[\left\{(\alpha+\beta)^2-2 \alpha \beta\right\}\right. \\
& \left.\left\{\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2\right)^2-3 \alpha^2 \beta^2\right\}-\alpha^3 \beta^3\right] \\
= & (\alpha+\beta) \left[(\alpha+\beta)^2-3 \alpha \beta\right]\left[\left\{(\alpha+\beta)^2-2 \alpha \beta\right\}\right. \\
& \left.\quad\left[ \left\{(\alpha+\beta)^2-(2 \alpha \beta)\right]^2-3 \alpha^2 \beta^2\right\}-\alpha^3 \beta^3\right]\\
= & 2[4-12]\left[\{4-8\}\left\{(4-8)^2-48\right\}-64\right]
\end{aligned} [from Eq. (i)] \begin{aligned}& =2(-8)\{(-4)(-32)(-64)\} \\
& =2(-8)(128-64) \\
& =2(-8)(64)=-2^{10}
\end{aligned}$

Now we have

$= \left(4{\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} - {\lambda}_{3}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(- {\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} - {\lambda}_{3}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- 3{\lambda}_{1} - {\lambda}_{2} + 2{\lambda}_{3}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$- {\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} - {\lambda}_{3} = 2 . . . \left(ii\right)$

$- 3{\lambda}_{1} - {\lambda}_{2} + 2{\lambda}_{3} = 3 . . . \left(iii\right)$

23280.subject: Physics
23280.text: The mass number of two nuclei $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ are 27 and 125 respectively. The ratio of their radii $R_P: R_Q$ is given by:
23280.sol:
The radius $R$ of a nucleus with mass number $A$ is given by the relation $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant.

For nucleus $\mathrm{P}$, $A_P = 27$. Thus, $R_P = R_0 (27)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 3$.

For nucleus $\mathrm{Q}$, $A_Q = 125$. Thus, $R_Q = R_0 (125)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 5$.

The ratio of their radii is $\dfrac{R_P}{R_Q} = \dfrac{R_0 \times 3}{R_0 \times 5} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Therefore, the ratio $R_P : R_Q$ is $3 : 5$.

Answer: 3 : 5

23375.subject: Physics
23375.text: When a particular wave length of light is used the focal length of a convex mirror is found to be $10 \mathrm{ cm}$. If the wave length of the incident light is doubled keeping the area of the mirror constant, the focal length of the mirror will be:
23375.sol:
The focal length $f$ of a spherical mirror is given by the relation $f = \dfrac{R}{2}$, where $R$ is the radius of curvature of the mirror.

The radius of curvature $R$ depends only on the geometry and the physical dimensions of the mirror surface. It is determined by the radius of the sphere from which the mirror is cut.

The focal length of a mirror is independent of the wavelength of the incident light. Changing the wavelength of the light does not alter the physical shape or the radius of curvature of the mirror.

Since the area of the mirror is kept constant, the radius of curvature $R$ remains unchanged. Therefore, the focal length remains $10 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: 10 cm

A source of sound emits sound waves at frequency $f_0$. It is moving towards an observer with fixed speed $v_s\left(v_s < v\right.$, where $v$ is the speed of sound in air.) The variation of $f$ with $v_0$ is given correctly by
23725.sol:
According to the Doppler effect, when a source of sound moving with speed $v_s$ towards a stationary observer emits sound of frequency $f_0$, and the observer moves towards the source with speed $v_0$, the observed frequency $f$ is given by the formula:

$f = f_0 \left( \dfrac{v + v_0}{v - v_s} \right)

where $v$ is the speed of sound in air. This equation can be rewritten as:

$f = $\left( \dfrac{f_0}{v - v_s} \right) v_0 + \left( \dfrac{f_0 v}{v - v_s} \right)$

This is a linear equation of the form $f = mv + c$, where $m$ is the slope and $c$ is the y-intercept. Comparing the terms, the slope $m$ is $\dfrac{f_0}{v - v_s}$ and the y-intercept $c$ is $\dfrac{f_0 v}{v - v_s}$.

Since the slope is a constant positive value, the graph of $f$ versus $v_0$ must be a straight line with a positive slope. Graph (a) represents a linear variation of $f$ with $v_0$. Therefore, graph (a) is the correct representation with a slope of $\dfrac{f_0}{v - v_s}$.

Answer: graph $A$ with slope $=\dfrac{f_0}{\left(v-v_s\right)}$

25625.text: For any $3 \times 3$ matrix $M$, let $| M |$ denote the determinant of $M$. Let $I$ be the $3 \times 3$ identity matrix. Let $E$ and $F$ be two $3 \times 3$ matrices such that $( I - EF )$ is invertible. If $G = ( I - EF{)}^{- 1}$, then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
25625.sol:
(A) $G = ( I - EF{)}^{- 1}$

$⇒ FGE = F ( I - EF{)}^{- 1}E$

$= {\left({E}^{- 1} ( I - EF ) {F}^{- 1}\right)}^{- 1}$

$⇒ FGE = {\left({E}^{- 1}{F}^{- 1} - I\right)}^{- 1}$

$⇒ | FGE | \cdot \left|{E}^{- 1}{F}^{- 1} - I\right| = 1$

$⇒ | FGE | \cdot \left|{E}^{- 1}{F}^{- 1} - I\right| | FE | = | FE |$

$⇒ | FGE | | I - FE | = | FE |$

(B) & (D) $( I - FE ) \cdot ( I + FGE )$

$= I + FGE - FE - FE \cdot FGE = 0$

$= I + FGE - FE - F ( G - I ) E$

$= I + FGE - FE - FGE + FE = I$

(C) $( I - EF ) G = I = G ( I - EFG )$

$⇒ G - EFG = I = G - GEF$

$⇒ EFG = GEF$

28141.text:
Consider the following gas phase reaction being carried out in a closed vessel at $25°C$.
$2A(g) \rightarrow 4B(g) + C(g)$
time (min)total pressure of the system (mm Hg)
$30$$300$
$\infty$$600$
The pressure of $C(g)$ at $30$ minutes time interval would be _______ mm Hg. (nearest integer)
28141.sol:
For the given gas phase reaction:

$2A(g) \rightarrow 4B(g) + C(g)$

Let the initial pressure of $A(g)$ be $P_0$.

At $t = 0$: $P_A = P_0$, $P_B = 0$, $P_C = 0$

At $t = t$: $P_A = P_0 - 2p$, $P_B = 4p$, $P_C = p$

Total pressure at time $t$, $P_t = P_0 - 2p + 4p + p = P_0 + 3p$

At $t = \infty$, the reaction is complete, so $P_A = 0 \Rightarrow 2p = P_0 \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{P_0}{2}$

Total pressure at $t = \infty$, $P_{\infty} = 4\left(\dfrac{P_0}{2}\right) + \dfrac{P_0}{2} = \dfrac{5P_0}{2}$

Given $P_{\infty} = 600$ mm Hg:

$\dfrac{5P_0}{2} = 600 \Rightarrow P_0 = 240$ mm Hg

At $t = 30$ min, $P_t = 300$ mm Hg:

$P_0 + 3p = 300$

$240 + 3p = 300 \Rightarrow 3p = 60 \Rightarrow p = 20$ mm Hg

The pressure of $C(g)$ at $30$ minutes is $p = 20$ mm Hg.

Answer: $20$

Initial temperature $= 300K$

$log2 = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{2 . 3R}\left[\dfrac{9}{300 \times 309}\right]$

${E}_{a} = \dfrac{2 . 3 \times 0 . 30 \times 300 \times 309}{9}$

${E}_{a} = 58 . 988 \times {10}^{3}J = 58 . 988kJ = 59kJ$

B. $Zn$ and $Cd$ do not show variable oxidation state while $Hg$ shows $+ I$ and $+ II$.
C. Compounds of $Zn, Cd$ and $Hg$ are paramagnetic in nature.
D. $Zn, Cd$ and $Hg$ are called soft metals.
Choose the most appropriate from the options given below:
29109.sol:
(A) $Zn, Cd$ and $Hg$ have low values of enthalpies of atomization. These metals have relatively weak metallic bonding due to their filled or nearly filled d-orbitals. In these metals, the valence electrons are not as delocalized as in other transition metals because the d-orbitals are filled or nearly filled. This leads to weaker metallic bonding, resulting in lower enthalpies compared to transition metals with partially filled d-orbitals. Thus statement (A) is incorrect.
(B) $Zn$ and $Cd$ shows $+ 2$ oxidation state whereas $Hg$ shows $+ 1$ and $+ 2$ oxidation state.Hence, statement (B) is correct.
(C) All electrons are paired in the compounds of zinc, cadmium and mercury. Hence, they are diamagnetic in nature. Hence, statement (C) is incorrect.
(D) $Zn, Cd$ and $Hg$ are soft metals as all electrons are paired and metallic bonds are not strong enough. Thus, statement (D) is correct.

So, $3 ( 2p - 9 ) < 0$

33350.text: If the coefficients of $x$ and ${x}^{2}$ in $( 1 + x{)}^{p} ( 1 - x{)}^{q}$ are $4$ and $- 5$ respectively, then $2p + 3q$ is equal to
33350.sol:
Given that The coefficient of $x$ and ${x}^{2}$ in ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{p}{\left(1 - x\right)}^{q}$ are $4$ and $- 5$.

$⇒ {\left(1 + x\right)}^{p}{\left(1 - x\right)}^{q} = \left(1 + px + \dfrac{p\left(p - 1\right)}{2 !}{x}^{2} + . . . .\right)\left(1 - qx + \dfrac{q\left(q - 1\right)}{2 !}{x}^{2} - . . . .\right)$

Now coefficient of $x$ from the above expansion will be

$p - q$ which is equal to $4$

$⇒ p - q = 4$.

Similarly coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ is $- 5$.

$⇒ \dfrac{p\left(p - 1\right)}{2} + \dfrac{q\left(q - 1\right)}{2} - pq = - 5$

$⇒ \dfrac{{p}^{2} - 2pq + {q}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{\left(p + q\right)}{2} = - 5$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(p - q\right)}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{\left(p + q\right)}{2} = - 5$

$⇒ \dfrac{16}{2} + 5 = \dfrac{\left(p + q\right)}{2}$

$⇒ p + q = 26$ and $p - q = 4$

On solving the above equations we get,

$p = 15$ and $q = 11$.

$⇒ 2p + 3q = 2\left(15\right) + 3\left(11\right) = 63$

Therefore, the required answer is $63$.

35849.sol:
To find $~ \left(p ↔ \left(q \to p\right)\right)$

We know $~ \left(p ↔ q\right) ≡ \left(p ∧ ~ q\right) ∨ \left(q ∧ ~ p\right)$

So $~ \left(p ↔ \left(q \to p\right)\right)$

$≡ \left(p ∧ ~ \left(q \to p\right)\right) ∨ \left(\left(q \to p\right) ∧ ~ p\right)$

Now $\left(p ∧ ~ \left(q \to p\right)\right) ≡ p ∧ \left(q ∧ ~ p\right) ≡ \left(p ∧ ~ p\right) ∧ q ≡ c$

and $\left(q \to p\right) ∧ ~ p ≡ \left(~ q ∨ p\right) ∧ ~ p ≡ ~ p ∧ \left(~ q ∨ p\right)$

$≡ \left(~ p ∧ ~ q\right) ∨ \left(~ p ∧ p\right) = ~ p ∧ ~ q$

Hence $~ \left(p ↔ \left(q \to p\right)\right) ≡ c ∨ \left(~ p ∧ ~ q\right) ≡ ~ p ∧ ~ q$

37285.text: The sum of all two digit positive numbers which when divided by $7$ yield $2$ or $5$ as remainder is
37285.sol:
Two-digit numbers of the form $7\lambda + 2$ are $16, 23, 30, . . . , 93$

These number are forming an arithmetic progression with first term $a = 16,$ common difference $d = 23 - 16 = 7$ and last term $l = 93$

And, we know that the last term of an arithmetic progression is given by $l = a + \left(n - 1\right)d$

$⇒ 93 = 16 + \left(n - 1\right)7$

$⇒ 77 = \left(n - 1\right)7$

$⇒ n = 12$

Two-digit numbers of the form $7\lambda + 5$ are $12, 19, 26, . . . , 96$

Again, using the last term of $A . P . ,$ we get $96 = 12 + \left({n}_{1} - 1\right)7$

$⇒ 84 = \left({n}_{1} - 1\right)7$

$⇒ {n}_{1} = 13$

Now, the sum of $n$ terms of an $A . P .$ is ${S}_{n} = \dfrac{n}{2}\left(a + l\right),$ we get the sum of all the above numbers as

$= \dfrac{12}{2}\left(16 + 93\right) + \dfrac{13}{2}\left(12 + 96\right)$

$= 654 + 702 = 1356 .$

40175.subject: Physics
40175.text:
The induced emf can be produced in a coil by

A. moving the coil with uniform speed inside uniform magnetic field

B. moving the coil with non uniform speed inside uniform magnetic field

C. rotating the coil inside the uniform magnetic field

D. changing the area of the coil inside the uniform magnetic field

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
40175.sol:
Induced emf is given by Faraday's law

$\left|ε\right| = \dfrac{dϕ}{dt}$

where $ϕ$ is the magnetic flux.

The rate of change of flux through a circuit is defined as emf. The formula for flux is $ϕ = \overset{\to}{B} \cdot \overset{\to}{A}$. In the statements $A \text{ and } B$ given in the question, the magnetic flux in the coil in uniform magnetic field does not change. So, no emf is induced.

But in statement $C$, the angle between the area vector and the magnetic field continuously changes hence, an emf is generated. In statement $D$, the area is changing in unit time so magnetic flux will change and an emf is generated.

40570.text: Three point charges of magnitude $5\muC, 0 . 16\muC$ and $0 . 3\muC$ are located at the vertices $A, B, C$ of a right angled triangle whose sides are $AB = 3cm$, $BC = 3\sqrt{2}cm$ and $CA = 3cm$ and point $A$ is the right angle corner. Charge at point $A$ experiences _____ $N$ of electrostatic force due to the other two charges.
40570.sol:
Using Coulomb's law the electrostatic force on& $A$~due to& $C$

${F}_{AC} = \dfrac{K{q}_{A}{q}_{C}}{\left({r}_{AC}\right)2} = \dfrac{k \times 5 \times 0 . 3 \times {10}^{- 12}}{9 \times {10}^{- 4}}= \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9} \times 5 \times 0 . 3 \times {10}^{- 12}}{9 \times {10}^{- 4}}$

$= 1 . 5 \times 10 = 15N$

Similarly, the force on~$A$~due to& $B$

${F}_{AB} = \dfrac{K{q}_{A}{q}_{B}}{\left({r}_{AB}\right)2} = \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9} \times 5 \times 0 . 16 \times {10}^{- 12}}{9 \times {10}^{- 4}} = 8N$

We can see that the forces are perpendicular to each other. Therefore, the net force experienced by charge at $A$~is,

$F = \sqrt{{FAC}^{2} + {FAB}^{2}}= \sqrt{{15}^{2} + {8}^{2}} = \sqrt{289} = 17N$

42191.subject: Physics
42191.text:
A particle starts moving from time $t=0$ and its coordinate is given as $x(t)=4 t^{3}-3 t$
A. The particle returns to its original position (origin) 0.866 units later
B. The particle is 1 unit away from origin at its turning point
C. Acceleration of the particle is non-negative
D. The particle is 0.5 units away from origin at its turning point
E. Particle never turns back as acceleration is non-negative
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
42191.sol:
Given $x(t) = 4t^3 - 3t$, we find $v(t) = 12t^2 - 3$ and $a(t) = 24t$.
Statement A: Setting $x(t) = 0$ gives $4t^3 - 3t = 0 \Rightarrow t(4t^2-3) = 0$, so $t = 0$ or $t = \sqrt{3/4} = 0.866$. The particle returns to origin at $t = 0.866$ units. TRUE.
Statement B: Turning points occur at $v(t) = 0 \Rightarrow 12t^2 - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow t = \pm 0.5$. At $t = 0.5$: $x = 4(0.125) - 1.5 = -1$; distance = 1 unit. At $t = -0.5$: $x = 1$; distance = 1 unit. TRUE.
Statement C: For $t \geq 0$ (particle starts at $t=0$), $a(t) = 24t \geq 0$. TRUE.
Statement D: At turning points, distance is 1 unit, not 0.5. FALSE.
Statement E: False because acceleration is non-negative only for $t \geq 0$, and particle does turn back at $t = 0.5$. FALSE.
Correct statements: A, B, C Only.

42499.subject: Physics
42499.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: For all elements, greater the mass of the nucleus, greater is the binding energy per nucleon.
Statement II: For all elements, nuclei with less binding energy per nucleon transforms to nuclei with greater binding energy per nucleon.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
42499.sol:
Statement I is false because binding energy per nucleon does not increase monotonically with mass number. It peaks at Iron-56 and decreases for heavier elements.
Statement II is true. It describes the fundamental principle of nuclear reactions: fission of heavy nuclei (low BE/A) and fusion of light nuclei (low BE/A) both produce nuclei with higher binding energy per nucleon, releasing energy in the process. Both processes are energetically favorable for the same reason: moving toward higher stability (higher BE/A).

The final kinetic energy of the pendulum at the lowermost position is given by

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

$\dfrac{9}{10}mgℓ = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{9}{10} \times 10 \times 10 = \dfrac{1}{2}{v}^{2} ⇒ {v}^{2} = 180 ⇒ v = \sqrt{180} = 6\sqrt{5}m{s}^{- 1}$

45069.subject: Botany
45069.text: The ability of the venus flytrap to capture insects is due to
options: a passive process requiring no special ability on the part of the plant
45069.sol: Insectivorous plants grow in water logged swampy soils, deficient in nitrogenous compounds. These plants obtain their nitrogen compounds from the insects. Due to this reason, these plants are called as semi-autotrophic or semi-heterotrophic. Dionea (an insectivorous plant) is commonly called as venus fly trap. Leaves of this plant have winged petiole and lamina modified into two toothed jaws. Each jaw bears several teeth. Upper surface of each jaw bears triangularly arranged long sensitive hairs or bristles and many glands, which are irregularly scattered. These hairs are very sensitive to touch stimulus. When an insect touches these hairs, this stimulus causes rapid turgor pressure changes which closes the leaf.

48766.text: One of the possible functions $f(x)$ which satisfies $\int\limits_{-2}^{2} f(x)\,dx = 0$ is
48766.sol: For an odd function $f(x)$, the definite integral over a symmetric interval is zero, i.e., $\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 0$.Let us check the function in the first option:$f(x) = \log \left(\dfrac{2 - x}{2 + x}\right)Substituting $-x$ for $x$, we get:$f(-x) = $\log\left(\dfrac{2 - (-x)}{2 + (-x)}\right) = \log\left(\dfrac{2 + x}{2 - x}\right)$Using the property of logarithms $\log(a^{-1}) = -\log(a)$:$f(-x) = \log\left(\left(\dfrac{2 - x}{2 + x}\right)^{-1}\right) = -\log\left(\dfrac{2 - x}{2 + x}\right) = -f(x)$Since $f(-x) = -f(x)$, the function $f(x) = \log \left(\dfrac{2 - x}{2 + x}\right)$ is an odd function.Therefore, $\int_{-2}^{2} \log\left(\dfrac{2 - x}{2 + x}\right)\,dx = 0$.Answer: $\log\left(\dfrac{2 - x}{2 + x}\right)$

& =3 \omega^2-3 \omega \\

54915.subject: Chemistry
54915.text: Which from following compounds is least soluble in water at STP?
54915.sol:
The solubility of substances in water is determined by their ability to form hydrogen bonds and interact with the polar solvent.

Ethanol ($\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}$) and methanol ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OH}$) contain hydroxyl groups that form strong hydrogen bonds with water.

Methylamine ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{NH}_2$) has an amino group capable of hydrogen bonding with water molecules.

Methane ($\mathrm{CH}_4$) is nonpolar with only weak London dispersion forces and cannot form hydrogen bonds, making it the least soluble compound.

Among these, methane exhibits the lowest solubility in water.

Final answer: $\boxed{D}$

57574.subject: Chemistry
57574.text: Which of the following alkyl halides undergoes $\text{SN}^1$ reaction most readily?
57574.sol:
The rate of an $\text{SN}^1$ reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation formed and the leaving group ability of the halide ion.

Since the alkyl group is the same in all the given options, the carbocation formed is the tert-butyl carbocation, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$, in each case.

The rate of reaction will therefore depend on the leaving group ability of the halide ion. A better leaving group leads to a faster reaction.

The leaving group ability increases as the size of the halogen atom increases and the carbon-halogen bond strength decreases. The order of bond dissociation energy is $\text{C-F} > \text{C-Cl} > \text{C-Br} > \text{C-I}$.

Thus, the iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) is the best leaving group among the halides.

Therefore, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I}$ undergoes the $\text{SN}^1$ reaction most readily.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I}$

$3\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_{3(aq)} + \text{BrO}_{3(aq)}^- \longrightarrow \text{Br}_{(aq)}^- + 3\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_{4(aq)}$
58608.sol:
The given reaction is $3\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_{3(aq)} + \text{BrO}_{3(aq)}^- \longrightarrow \text{Br}_{(aq)}^- + 3\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_{4(aq)}$

Let the oxidation state of As in $\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_3$ be $x$.
$3(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3$

Let the oxidation state of Br in $\text{BrO}_3^-$ be $y$.
$y + 3(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow y = +5$

Let the oxidation state of As in $\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_4$ be $z$.
$3(+1) + z + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow z = +5$

The oxidation state of Br in $\text{Br}^-$ is $-1$.

The oxidation state of As increases from $+3$ to $+5$, so $\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_3$ undergoes oxidation and acts as a reducing agent.

The oxidation state of Br decreases from $+5$ to $-1$, so $\text{BrO}_3^-$ undergoes reduction and acts as an oxidising agent.

The change in oxidation state of the oxidising agent is $+5$ to $-1$.

Answer: $+5\ \text{to}\ -1$

58793.subject: Chemistry
58793.text: A metal crystallizes in a bcc unit cell having unit cell volume $2.5 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$. Find the number of unit cells in 18 g metal if the density of metal is $7.2\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$.
58793.sol:
Total volume of the metal is given by the ratio of mass to density.

$V_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}} = \dfrac{18}{7.2} = 2.5\ \text{cm}^3$

The number of unit cells is the total volume divided by the volume of one unit cell.

$\text{Number of unit cells} = \dfrac{V_{\text{total}}}{V_{\text{unit cell}}} = \dfrac{2.5}{2.5 \times 10^{-23}} = 1.0 \times 10^{23}$

Answer: $1.0 \times 10^{23}$

Let $y = \sin\left(\log\left(\dfrac{x+3}{x}\right)\right)$

Using the chain rule, differentiating with respect to $x$ gives:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos\left(\log\left(\dfrac{x+3}{x}\right)\right) \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\log\left(\dfrac{x+3}{x}\right)\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos\left(\log\left(\dfrac{x+3}{x}\right)\right) \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(\log(x+3) - \log x)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos\left(\log\left(\dfrac{x+3}{x}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{x - (x+3)}{x(x+3)}\right)$

62717.text: The value of $\lim_{x \to 3} \dfrac{[x] - 3}{x - 3}$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is.....
62717.sol:
Evaluate the left-hand limit (LHL) and right-hand limit (RHL) at $x = 3$.

For LHL, let $x \to 3^{-}$. Then $[x] = 2$.

LHL $= \lim_{x \to 3^{-}} \dfrac{[x] - 3}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^{-}} \dfrac{2 - 3}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^{-}} \dfrac{-1}{x - 3} = \infty$

For RHL, let $x \to 3^{+}$. Then $[x] = 3$.

RHL $= \lim_{x \to 3^{+}} \dfrac{[x] - 3}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^{+}} \dfrac{3 - 3}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^{+}} 0 = 0$

Since LHL ≠ RHL, the limit does not exist.

Answer: does not exist

66319.subject: Physics
66319.text: Two wires A and B of equal lengths are connected in left and right gap respectively of a metre bridge, null point is obtained at 40 cm from left end. Diameters of the wires A and B are in the ratio 3:1 respectively, the ratio of specific resistance of A to that of B is
66319.sol:
Using the principle of a metre bridge, the ratio of resistances in the left and right gaps is given by

$\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \dfrac{l}{100 - l}$

Substituting $l = 40$ cm, we get

$\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \dfrac{40}{100 - 40} = \dfrac{40}{60} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

The resistance of a wire is given by $R = \rho \dfrac{L}{A} = \rho \dfrac{4L}{\pi d^2}$, where $\rho$ is the specific resistance, $L$ is the length, and $d$ is the diameter.

Since the lengths of wires A and B are equal, the ratio of their resistances is

$\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \left(\dfrac{\rho_A}{\rho_B}\right) \left(\dfrac{d_B}{d_A}\right)^2$

Given that the ratio of diameters is $\dfrac{d_A}{d_B} = \dfrac{3}{1}$, we have $\dfrac{d_B}{d_A} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Substituting the values into the resistance ratio equation:

$\dfrac{2}{3} = \left(\dfrac{\rho_A}{\rho_B}\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2$

$\dfrac{2}{3} = \left(\dfrac{\rho_A}{\rho_B}\right) \times \dfrac{1}{9}$

$\dfrac{\rho_A}{\rho_B} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 9 = 6$

The ratio of specific resistance of A to that of B is $6 : 1$.

Answer: $6 : 1$

66565.text:
The wavelength ' $\lambda$ ' of a photon and the de-Broglie wavelength of an electron have same value. the ratio of kinetic energy of the electron to the energy of a photon is
( $\mathrm{m}=$ mass of electron, $\mathrm{c}=$ velocity of light, $\mathrm{h}=$ Planck's constant)
66565.sol:
For an electron and photon with equal wavelengths $\lambda_e = \lambda_{ph} = \lambda$, the de Broglie relation gives the electron's momentum as $p_e = h/\lambda$.

The kinetic energy of the electron is $KE_e = p_e^2 / (2m) = h^2 / (2m\lambda^2)$.

The photon energy is $E_{ph} = hc/\lambda$.

The ratio of kinetic energies simplifies to:

$\frac{KE_e}{E_{ph}} = \frac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2} \cdot \frac{\lambda}{hc} = \frac{h}{2m\lambda c}$

This corresponds to option C.

68012.subject: Physics
68012.text: The length of a cylinder is measured with a meter rod having least count $0.1$ cm. Its diameter is measured with vernier calipers having least count $0.01$ cm. Length of cylinder is $8.0$ cm and radius is $4.0$ cm. Find the percentage error in the calculated value of the volume.
68012.sol:
The volume of a cylinder is given by $V = \pi R^2 L$.

Since the diameter $D$ is measured, we can write the volume in terms of diameter as $V = \dfrac{\pi D^2 L}{4}$.

The maximum percentage error in the volume is given by:
$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( 2 \dfrac{\Delta D}{D} + \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \right) \times 100$

Given values:
Length of the cylinder, $L = 8.0$ cm
Least count of meter rod, $\Delta L = 0.1$ cm
Radius of the cylinder, $R = 4.0$ cm \Rightarrow Diameter, $ D = 2R = 8.0$ cm
Least count of vernier calipers, $\Delta D = 0.01$ cm

Substituting these values into the percentage error formula:
$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( 2 \times \dfrac{0.01}{8.0} + \dfrac{0.1}{8.0} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{0.02}{8.0} + \dfrac{0.1}{8.0} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{0.12}{8.0} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \dfrac{12}{8.0} = 1.5\%$

Answer: $1.5\%$

$⇒ d = \sqrt{\dfrac{4M\left(g \pm a\right)}{\piS}}$
As acceleration is maximum i.e.’=g +a, so
$d = \sqrt{\dfrac{4M\left(g + a\right)}{\piS}}$

68451.subject: Physics
68451.text: Two bodies A and B move in same straight line starting from same position. Body A moves with constant velocity 'u' and body B moves with constant acceleration ' $a$ '. When their velocities become equal, the distance between them is
68451.sol:
Define $x=0$ as the initial position at $t=0$. Body A moves with constant velocity $v_A = u$, so its position is $x_A = u t$. Body B accelerates from rest with constant acceleration $a$, giving velocity $v_B = a t$ and position $x_B = \frac{1}{2} a t^2$.

Equate their velocities to find when they are equal: $u = a t$, so $t = \frac{u}{a}$.

At this time, $x_A = u \cdot \frac{u}{a} = \frac{u^2}{a}$ and $x_B = \frac{1}{2} a \left( \frac{u}{a} \right)^2 = \frac{u^2}{2a}$. The distance between them is the absolute difference, which simplifies to $D = \left| \frac{u^2}{a} - \frac{u^2}{2a} \right| = \frac{u^2}{2a}$.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

68716.subject: Physics
68716.text: A mass $m$ is suspended from a spring of negligible mass. The spring is pulled a little and then released, so that mass executes S.H.M. of time period T . If the mass is increased by $\mathrm{m}_0$, the periodic time becomes $\frac{5 \mathrm{ T}}{4}$. The ratio $\frac{\mathrm{m}_0}{\mathrm{M}}$ is
68716.sol:
The period of oscillation for a mass-spring system is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}$.

When the mass increases to $m + m_0$, the new period becomes $T' = \frac{5T}{4}$.

Taking the ratio of periods:

$\frac{T'}{T} = \sqrt{\frac{m + m_0}{m}}$

Substituting $T' = \frac{5T}{4}$ yields:

$\frac{5}{4} = \sqrt{\frac{m + m_0}{m}}$

Squaring both sides:

$\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{m + m_0}{m}$

Which simplifies to:

$\frac{25}{16} = 1 + \frac{m_0}{m}$

Solving for the ratio:

$\frac{m_0}{m} = \frac{25}{16} - 1 = \frac{9}{16}$

The ratio of additional mass to original mass is $\frac{9}{16}$.

69146.subject: Physics
69146.text: A solid sphere rolls down from the top of an inclined plane. On reaching the bottom of the plane, its velocity is '$V_1$'. When the same sphere slides down from the top of the same plane of same height, its velocity on reaching the bottom is '$V_2$'. The ratio $V_1 : V_2$ is (neglect friction)
69146.sol:
When a solid sphere rolls down an inclined plane of height $h$, by conservation of mechanical energy:

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mV_1^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2$

For a solid sphere, the moment of inertia is $I = \dfrac{2}{5}mr^2$ and for pure rolling, $\omega = \dfrac{V_1}{r}$.

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mV_1^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}mr^2\right)\left(\dfrac{V_1}{r}\right)^2$

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mV_1^2 + \dfrac{1}{5}mV_1^2 = \dfrac{7}{10}mV_1^2$

$V_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{10gh}{7}}$

When the sphere slides down the same plane without friction, it only acquires translational kinetic energy. By conservation of mechanical energy:

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mV_2^2$

$V_2 = \sqrt{2gh}$

The ratio of the velocities is:

$\dfrac{V_1}{V_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{10gh}{7}}}{\sqrt{2gh}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{10}{7 \times 2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{7}}$

Thus, $V_1 : V_2 = \sqrt{5} : \sqrt{7}$.

69173.subject: Physics
69173.text: A body slides down a smooth inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ and reaches the bottom with velocity 'V'. If the same body is a ring which rolls down the same inclined plane then linear velocity at the bottom of the plane is
69173.sol:
Let the height of the inclined plane be $h$.

For the body sliding down the smooth inclined plane, the conservation of mechanical energy gives:

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mV^2$

$V = \sqrt{2gh}$

For the ring rolling down the same inclined plane, the total kinetic energy at the bottom is the sum of translational and rotational kinetic energy:

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2$

For a ring, the moment of inertia is $I = mR^2$ and for pure rolling, $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$. Substituting these values:

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}(mR^2)\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)^2$

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = mv^2$

$v = \sqrt{gh}$

Comparing the two velocities:

$v = \dfrac{\sqrt{2gh}}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{2}}$

71132.subject: Biology
71132.text: Find the drug from the options given below, which is extracted from the latex of Papaver somniferum?
71132.sol:
Opioids are drugs that bind to specific opioid receptors present in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract.

Heroin, commonly called smack, is chemically diacetylmorphine. It is a white, odourless, bitter crystalline compound.

Smack is obtained by the acetylation of morphine, which is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant Papaver somniferum.

Hashish and Charas are cannabinoids obtained from the inflorescences of the plant Cannabis sativa.

LSD (Lysergic acid diethylamide) is extracted from the fruiting body of the fungus Claviceps purpurea.

Answer: Smack

71161.subject: Biology
71161.text:
Given below are two statements related to drugs abuse:
Statement (I): Excessive dosage of cocaine causes extreme happiness, irritability, paranoia etc.
Statement (II): A drug like heroin obtained from Cannabis sativa is used as depressant as it slows down the activity of body.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71161.sol:
Statement (I) is incorrect. According to NCERT, cocaine has a potent stimulating action on the central nervous system, producing a sense of euphoria (extreme happiness) and increased energy at normal doses. However, an excessive dosage of cocaine causes hallucinations.

Statement (II) is incorrect. Heroin is a depressant and slows down body functions, but it is obtained from the acetylation of morphine, which is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant (Papaver somniferum). Cannabis sativa is the source of cannabinoids (such as marijuana, hashish, charas, and ganja), not heroin.

Therefore, both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.

Answer: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.

71220.subject: Biology
71220.text: Which one of the following biofertilizer makes the plant associated with them grow luxuriantly in less irrigated lands?
71220.sol:
Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhizae (VAM) are symbiotic associations between fungi and the roots of higher plants. The fungal hyphae extend into the soil, significantly increasing the surface area for absorption. This allows the plant to absorb water and essential nutrients, particularly phosphorus, more efficiently from the soil. Due to this enhanced water uptake capability, plants associated with VAM can grow luxuriantly even in less irrigated or drought-prone lands.

Answer: Vesiculo Arbuscular Mycorrhizae

71508.subject: Biology
71508.text: Which one of the following is of great significance in horticulture?
71508.sol:
Nucellar adventive polyembryony is of great significance in horticulture. In this process, embryos develop directly from the nucellus or integument cells, which are maternal tissues. As a result, the embryos are genetically identical to the parent plant, ensuring the preservation of desirable traits (clonal propagation). Furthermore, seedlings raised from nucellar embryos are generally free from viruses and exhibit higher vigour compared to those produced through vegetative propagation methods like cuttings. This is extensively utilized in the cultivation of crops like Citrus and Mango.

Answer: Nucellar adventive polyembryony.

72268.subject: Physics
72268.text:
If the current 'i' is passing through the wire, it has a shape as shown in the figure. The radius of the curved part is R and the linear part is assumed to be very long. The magnetic induction of the field at the point O, is
(\mu_0=$permeability of free space)
$
72268.sol:
The wire can be divided into three parts: a lower semi-infinite straight wire, a semicircular arc, and an upper semi-infinite straight wire.

The magnetic field at point O due to the lower semi-infinite straight wire is given by $B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}$. Applying the right-hand rule, the current is towards the left and point O is above the wire, so the magnetic field is directed into the page.

The magnetic field at point O due to the semicircular arc is given by $B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R} = \dfrac{\pi \mu_0 i}{4\pi R}$. The current is in the clockwise direction, so the magnetic field is directed into the page.

The magnetic field at point O due to the upper semi-infinite straight wire is given by $B_3 = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}$. The current is towards the right and point O is below the wire, so the magnetic field is directed into the page.

Since all three magnetic field components are in the same direction, the total magnetic field at O is their sum:

$B_{net} = B_1 + B_2 + B_3$

$B_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R} + \dfrac{\pi \mu_0 i}{4\pi R} + \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}$

$B_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}(1 + \pi + 1)$

$B_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}(2 + \pi)$

77933.subject: Mathematics
77933.text: The probability that in a random arrangement of the letters of the word 'UNIVERSITY' the two I's do not come together is
77933.sol:
The total number of arrangements of the letters of the word 'UNIVERSITY' is $\frac{10!}{2!}$ as there are two I's.
Regarding 2I's as one letter, number of ways of arrangement in which both I's are together $=9$ !
So, the number of ways in which 2 I's are not together
$=\frac{10!}{2!}-9!$
Hence, the required probability
$=\frac{\frac{10!}{2!}-9!}{\frac{10!}{2!}}=1-\frac{2!9!}{10!}=\frac{4}{5}$.

78341.subject: Mathematics
78341.text: The sum of the first 8 terms of a GP is five times the sum of its first 4 terms. If $r \neq 1$ is the common ratio, then what is the number of possible real values of $r$?
78341.sol:
Let the first term of the GP be $a$ and the common ratio be $r$.

The sum of the first $n$ terms is given by $S_n = \dfrac{a(r^n - 1)}{r - 1}$.

According to the given condition, $S_8 = 5S_4$.

$\dfrac{a(r^8 - 1)}{r - 1} = 5 \dfrac{a(r^4 - 1)}{r - 1}$

For a non-zero first term $a$ and given $r \neq 1$:

$r^8 - 1 = 5(r^4 - 1)$

$(r^4 - 1)(r^4 + 1) = 5(r^4 - 1)$

Assuming $r^4 - 1 \neq 0$ to avoid the trivial zero-sum case:

$r^4 + 1 = 5$

$r^4 = 4$

Since $r$ is a real number, $r^2$ must be positive.

$r^2 = 2$

$r = \pm\sqrt{2}$

Therefore, there are two possible real values of $r$.

79117.subject: Mathematics
79117.text:
Consider the function $f(\theta)=4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^4 \theta\right)$
Consider the following statements:
1. $f(\theta)=2$ has no solution.
2. $\mathrm{f}(\theta)=\frac{7}{2}$ has a solution.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
79117.sol:
$\begin{aligned} f(\theta)= & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^4 \theta\right) \\ = & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\left(1-\sin ^2 \theta\right)\right) \\ = & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta \cos ^2 \theta\right) \\ = & 4\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right) \\ & {[\because \sin 2 \theta=2 \sin \theta \cos \theta] }\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& f(\theta)=2 \\
& 4\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right)=2 \\
& \Rightarrow 1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=\frac{2}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=+\frac{1}{2}-1 \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=-\frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin ^2 2 \theta=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta= \pm \sqrt{2}
\end{aligned}$
Since $\sin \theta$ cannot have vlaue greater than $1$ $\&$ less than -1.
Hence $f(\theta)=2$ has no solution.
$\begin{aligned} & f(\theta)=\frac{7}{2} \\ & 4\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right)=\frac{7}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right)=\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=\frac{7}{8}-1 \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=-\frac{1}{8} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin ^2 2 \theta=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta= \pm \sin \frac{\pi}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta=\sin ( \pm \pi / 4) \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \theta= \pm \pi / 4 \\
& \theta=( \pm) \frac{\pi}{8}
\end{aligned}$
Hence $f(\theta)=\frac{7}{2}$ has a solution.

79973.text: Quercus species are the dominant component in
79973.sol:
Temperate deciduous forests grow in continental climates with summer rainfall and severe winters. They are dominated by broad leaved deciduous trees like Quercus virginiana, magnolias, boys and hallies as well as such tropical species as Ficus aurea, Lysiloma.
Tropical rain forests occupy low altitude zones near the equator where annual rainfall exceeds $80^{\prime \prime}$ to $90^{\prime \prime}$ distributed over the year. Trees generally form three storeys scattered very tall emergent trees, canopy layer and understorey stratum.
Tropical scrub forests develop in areas where moisture relations are intermediate between desert and savanna on one hand and rainforest on other.

80041.subject: Botany
80041.text: Nitrogen-fixation in root nodules of Alnus is brought about by
80041.sol:
Nitrogen is the most critical element. Atmosphere is the greatest reservior of nitrogen. Molecular nitrogen cannot be utilized directly by plants. It has to be fixed or converted into compounds prior to utilization. symbiotic nitrogen fixation is accomplished by Rhizobium species, which occurs on the roots of leguminous plants. Certain non-leguminous plants also form nodules to fix nitrogen. The best known example in temperate region is alder (Alnus sp.). The bacteria involved in nodule formation is an Actinomycetes, the Frankia.
Clostridium is anaerobic, saprotrophic, free-living nitrogen fixing bacteria.
Bradyrhizobium is symbiont in plants of Parasponia and soybean.
The Azorhizobium forms both stem and root nodules in Sesbania (aquatic plant).

Chlorine and iodine are used as strong disinfectants

81108.sol:
Antiseptics and disinfectants both either kill or prevent the growth of microorganisms. The main point of difference between these two is that the former (antiseptics) are used for living beings whereas disinfectants are not safe for living tissues. These are actually used for inanimate objects like floors, tiles etc.
A substance like phenol in its lower concentration $(0.2 \%)$ behaves as antiseptic wheras in higher concentration (1\%) as disinfectant. Chlorine and iodine are strong disinfectants whereas dilute solutions of boric acid and hydrogen peroxide are mild antiseptics.

84206.subject: Zoology
84206.text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.

Column-I Column-II
(a) Pituitary gland (i) Grave’s disease
(b) Thyroid gland (ii) Diabetes mellitus
(c) Adrenal gland (iii) Diabetes insipidus
(d) Pancreas (iv) Addison’s disease
84206.sol:
Grave's disease: Due to cancer of the thyroid gland, due to development of nodules of the thyroid glands, or due to autoimmunity, the rate of synthesis and secretion of the thyroid hormones is increased to abnormally high levels leading to a condition called hyperthyroidism which adversely affects the body physiology. It leads to Grave’s disease or exophthalmic goiter. It causes weight loss, increased metabolism, rapid reflexes, nervousness, etc.

Diabetes mellitus: It is caused due to insulin deficiency or hypofunctioning of beta cells of Islets of Langerhans of the pancreas. Urine is sweet to taste due to the presence of sugar. Due to the presence of sugar, there is failure in normal osmotic reabsorption of water by kidney tubules.

Diabetes insipidus: It is caused due to deficiency of ADH or hypofunctioning of the pituitary. Sugar is generally absent in urine. Absence of ADH decreases the permeability of collecting tubule.

Addison's disease: It is caused due to hypofunctioning of adrenal or suprarenal glands or due to deficiency of cortisol and sometimes aldosterone too.

85116.subject: Zoology
85116.text: The logistic population growth is expressed by the equation
85116.sol:
A population growing in a habitat with limited resources show initially a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration and finally an asymptote, when the population density reaches the carrying capacity. A plot of $\mathrm{N}$ (population density at time $t$ ) in relation to time (t) results in sigmoid curve. This type of population grown is called Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth and is describes by the following equation : $d N / d t=r N\left(\frac{K-N}{K}\right)$ where, $N=$ Population density at time $t$, $r=$ Intrinsic rate of natural increase $K$ = Carrying capacity
Since resources for growth for most animal populations are finite and become limiting soner or later, the logistic growth model is considered a more realistic one.

s3 = 8.0 × 10-9

91605.text: An unbiased die is rolled until a number greater than $4$ appears. The probability that an even number of trials are needed, is
91605.sol:
$p$ = Probability of success $\left(s\right)$~$= \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$q$ = Probability of failure $\left(f\right)$~$= 1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

The probability that success occurs in even number of trials

$= p ( fs ) + p ( fffs ) + p ( fffffs ) + . . . . .$

$= \text{qp} + q^{3}\text{p} + q^{5}\text{p} + \ldots = \dfrac{qp}{1 - q^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{3}}{1 - {\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2}{9}}{1 - \dfrac{4}{9}} = \dfrac{2}{9} \times \dfrac{9}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

91705.text: If one root of the equation $x^{2} + px + q = 0$ & is the square of the other, then
91705.sol:
$x^{2} + px + q = 0$

Let, $\alpha , {\alpha}^{2}$ are the roots of the given equation.

$⇒ \alpha + {\alpha}^{2} = - p$

and $\alpha \cdot {\alpha}^{2} = q$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{3} = q$

$∵ \alpha + {\alpha}^{2} = - p$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha + {\alpha}^{2}\right)}^{3} = - p^{3}$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{6} + {\alpha}^{3} + 3\alpha.{\alpha}^{2}\left(\alpha + {\alpha}^{2}\right) = - p^{3}$

$⇒ q^{2} + q + 3 {\alpha}^{3} \left(\alpha + {\alpha}^{2}\right) = - p^{3}$

$⇒ q^{2} + q + 3 q \left(- p\right) = - p^{3}$

$⇒ p^{3} + q^{2} + q - 3pq = 0$

$⇒ p^{3} + q^{2} + q \left(1 - 3 p\right) = 0$

91724.text: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} + ax + 1 = 0, a \ne 0 .$ Then the equation whose roots are $- \left(\alpha + \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)$ and $- \left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \beta\right)$ is
91724.sol:
$\alpha + \beta = - a$ and $\alpha\beta = 1$
Let $S$ and $P$ be the sum and product of the roots of the required equation. Then,
$S = - \alpha - \dfrac{1}{\beta} - \dfrac{1}{\alpha} - \beta = - ( \alpha + \beta ) - \left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)$
$= - ( \alpha + \beta ) - \left(\dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{\alpha\beta}\right) = - ( - a ) - \left(\dfrac{- a}{1}\right) = 2a$
$P = - \left(\alpha + \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)\left(- \left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \beta\right)\right)$
$= 1 + \alpha\beta + \dfrac{1}{\alpha\beta} + 1 = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4$
So, the required equation is
${x}^{2} - Sx + P = 0$
i.e. ${x}^{2} - 2ax + 4 = 0$

92436.text: Let $\overset{\to}{PR} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{SQ} = \overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$ represent the diagonals of the parallelogram $PQRS$. If $\overset{\to}{PT} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is another vector, then the volume (in cubic units) of the parallelepiped formed by the vectors $\overset{\to}{PT}, \overset{\to}{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to}{PS}$ is
92436.sol:
Here,

$\begin{array}{ll}\overset{\to}{PQ} + \overset{\to}{PS} = \overset{\to}{PR} \\ \overset{\to}{PQ} - \overset{\to}{PS} = \overset{\to}{SQ}\end{array}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PQ} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\overset{\to}{PR} + \overset{\to}{SQ}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PQ} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

Also, $\overset{\to}{PS} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\overset{\to}{PR} - \overset{\to}{SQ}\right)$

$= \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Volume of parallelepiped $= \left[\overset{\to}{PT}\overset{\to}{PQ}\overset{\to}{PS}\right]$

$= \left|\begin{cases}2 & - 1 & 1 \\ 2 & - 1 & - 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= 2\left(5\right) + 1\left(5\right) + 1\left(5\right) = 20$ cubic units

Now, ${y}_{cm} = \dfrac{{m}_{1}{y}_{1} + {m}_{2}{y}_{2}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2}}$

Therefore, $0 = \left(m / 4\right) \left(+15\right) + \left(3m / 4\right)\left(y\right)\left(m / 4 + 3m / 4\right)$

or, $y = - 5\text{cm}$

∴ ${ω}^{2} = \dfrac{{k}_{1} a^{2} + {k}_{2} b^{2}}{L^{2} \left(\text{m} + \dfrac{\text{M}}{3}\right)}$



Hence, frequency

$\text{f} = \dfrac{2}{\pi} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{1} a^{2} + {k}_{2} b^{2}}{L^{2} \left(\text{m} + \dfrac{\text{M}}{3}\right)}}$

Also, we know that
$\beta = \dfrac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha}$
$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{\dfrac{7.9}{8}}{1 - \dfrac{7.9}{8}} = \dfrac{7.9}{8 - 7.9}$
$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{7.9}{0.1} = 79$
Hence, the required answer is $\alpha = 0. 99$ and $\beta = 79$.

94963.text: An interference is observed due to two coherent sources $A$ and $B$ separated by a distance $4\lambda$ along Y-axis where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of the light source used. A detector $D$ is moved along the positive X-axis. Find the total number of maxima points are observed on the X-axis excluding the points $x = 0$ and $x = \infty$?
94963.sol:
To obtain maxima the path difference

$AD - BD = n\lambda$

$AD - {x}_{n} = n\lambda$

$AD = n\lambda + {x}_{n}$ ...(i)

Form ${∆}_{le}$ ABD,

$A{D}^{2} = A{B}^{2} + B{D}^{2}$

${\left(n\lambda + {x}_{n}\right)}^{2} = 16{\lambda}^{2} + {x}_{n}^{2}$

${n}^{2}{\lambda}^{2} + {x}_{n}^{2} + 2n\lambda{x}_{n} = 16{\lambda}^{2} + {x}_{n}^{2}$

$2n\lambda{x}_{n} = \left(16 - {n}^{2}\right){\lambda}^{2}$

${x}_{n} = \dfrac{\left(16 - {n}^{2}\right)\lambda}{2n}$

For $n = 0 ⇒ {x}_{0} = \infty$

$n = 1 ⇒ {x}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{16 - 1}{2}\right)\lambda = \dfrac{15\lambda}{2} = 7.5\lambda$

$n = 2 ⇒ {x}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{16 - 1}{2}\right)\lambda = \dfrac{12\lambda}{4} = 3\lambda$

$n = 3 ⇒ {x}_{3} = \left(\dfrac{16 - 9}{6}\right)\lambda = \dfrac{7\lambda}{6}$

$n = 4 ⇒ {x}_{4} = \left(\dfrac{16 - 16}{2 \times 4}\right)\lambda = 0$

So the total no. of maxima points observed are 3.

options: Carbon cycle is imperfect cycle while phosphorus cycle is perfect cycle.
Ten percent law was proposed by Odum in 1942.
Grazing food chain helps in releasing inorganic nutrients to the cycling pool.
Seral community is a transitional community which develops in an area during succession.
96607.sol:
The process of the changes occurring in the structure of various organisms in an ecosystem over a period of time is referred to as ecological succession. During ecological succession, one of the intermediate stages that develops is called the seral community. It gets replaced by a successive community during the succession process.

The phosphorus cycle is considered as an imperfect cycle as the phosphorus that originates from a source does not go back to it. Lindemann proposed the Ten Percent Law for energy transfer in an ecosystem. Detritus food chain starts with dead organic matter where the organic matter is decomposed to its inorganic content and made available for the producers in the ecosystem.

97870.sol:
Taxonomy is the branch of biological science which includes nomenclature and classification of the organisms into groups based on their shared features and characteristics.

Classification is the process of grouping organisms based on observable features in to categories called 'taxa'. This process involves hierarchy of steps where each taxa represents a rank. All the steps/taxon collectively is referred as taxonomic hierarchy. The ranks/taxa have the following sequence from largest to the smallest with similarities in organisms increasing at each step. 100412.subject: Physics
100412.text:
A particle moves along a straight line $O X$. At a time $t$ (in second) the distance $x$ (in metre) of the particle from $O$ is given by
$x=40+12 t-t^3$
How long would the particle travel before coming to rest?
100412.sol:
Key Idea : Speed is rate of change of distance. Distance travelled by the particle is
$x=40+12 t-t^3$
We know that, speed is rate of change of distance $i e, v=\frac{d x}{d t} \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad v & =\frac{d}{d t}\left(40+12 t-t^3\right) \\ & =0+12-3 t^2\end{aligned}$
but final velocity $v=0 \therefore \quad 12-3 t^2=0$ or $\quad t^2=\frac{12}{3}=4
or t=2 \mathrm{~s}$
Hence, distance travelled by the particle before coming to rest is given by
$\begin{aligned} x & =40+12(2)-(2)^3 \\ & =40+24-8=64-8 \\ & =56 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

100916.subject: Physics
100916.text: A particle of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ moves along the x-axis. Its position varies with time according to the equation $x = t^3 + t$, where $x$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds. The instantaneous power delivered to the particle by the net force at $t = 2 \text{ s}$ is:
100916.sol:
Given, position of the particle is $x = t^3 + t$

Velocity of the particle is:
$v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(t^3 + t) = 3t^2 + 1$

Acceleration of the particle is:
$a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(3t^2 + 1) = 6t$

At $t = 2 \text{ s}$:
$v = 3(2)^2 + 1 = 13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$
$a = 6(2) = 12 \text{ m s}^{-2}$

According to Newton's second law, the net force acting on the particle is:
$F = ma = 2 \times 12 = 24 \text{ N}$

The instantaneous power delivered by the net force is:
$P = Fv = 24 \times 13 = 312 \text{ W}$

Answer: $312 \text{ W}$

101884.subject: Physics
101884.text: A lake is covered by an ice layer of thickness $x$ having thermal conductivity $K_1$. On top of this ice is a uniform layer of snow of thickness $y$ having thermal conductivity $K_2$. The air above the snow is at a steady temperature of $-\theta^\circ\text{C}$. If $\rho$ is the density of water and $L$ is its specific latent heat of fusion, the rate of increase of the ice layer thickness $\left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right)$ is given by
options: $\dfrac{\theta(K_1 y + K_2 x)}{\rho L x y}$
101884.sol:
The heat must conduct through both the ice layer and the snow layer in series.

The thermal resistance of the ice layer is $R_1 = \dfrac{x}{K_1 A}$ and that of the snow layer is $R_2 = \dfrac{y}{K_2 A}$.

The equivalent thermal resistance of the composite slab is $R_{eq} = R_1 + R_2 = \dfrac{1}{A} \left( \dfrac{x}{K_1} + \dfrac{y}{K_2} \right)$.

The temperature difference across the layers is $\Delta \theta = 0^\circ\text{C} - (-\theta^\circ\text{C}) = \theta$.

The rate of heat flow is $\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{\theta A}{\dfrac{x}{K_1} + \dfrac{y}{K_2}}$.

The rate at which heat is released due to the freezing of water is $\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \rho A L \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

Equating the two expressions for the rate of heat flow, we get:

$\rho A L \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{\theta A}{\dfrac{x}{K_1} + \dfrac{y}{K_2}}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{\theta}{\rho L \left( \dfrac{x}{K_1} + \dfrac{y}{K_2} \right)}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\theta}{\rho L \left(\dfrac{x}{K_1} + \dfrac{y}{K_2}\right)}$

104473.subject: Physics
104473.text: A convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ and a concave lens of focal length $10\text{ cm}$ are placed in contact. An object is placed $40\text{ cm}$ in front of this lens combination. At what distance from the combination will the image be formed?
options: $40\text{ cm}$ on the same side as the object
$\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$ on the same side as the object
$\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$ on the opposite side of the object
$8\text{ cm}$ on the opposite side of the object
104473.sol:
First, find the equivalent focal length ($F_{eq}$) of the lens combination.
For the convex lens, $f_1 = +20\text{ cm}$.
For the concave lens, $f_2 = -10\text{ cm}$.

$\dfrac{1}{F_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\dfrac{1}{F_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1 - 2}{20} = -\dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$
So, $F_{eq} = -20\text{ cm}$ (the combination acts as a concave lens).

Next, apply the thin lens formula to find the image position ($v$).
Object distance, $u = -40\text{ cm}$.

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{F_{eq}}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-40} = \dfrac{1}{-20}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{40} = -\dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = -\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{-2 - 1}{40} = -\dfrac{3}{40}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

$v = -\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$

The negative sign indicates that the image is formed on the same side as the object, at a distance of $\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$ from the lens combination.

Answer: $\dfrac{40}{3}\text{ cm}$ on the same side as the object

104497.subject: Physics
104497.text:
An object is placed at $x = -30$ cm on the principal axis of a coordinate system. A convex lens $L_1$ of focal length $20$ cm is fixed at the origin ($x = 0$). A second lens $L_2$ is placed at $x = +30$ cm. Match the specifications of lens $L_2$ in List-I with the x-coordinate of the final image in List-II.

List-I (Lens $L_2$)List-II (Final image position)
(A) Convex, $f = +15$ cm(I) $x = 0$ cm
(B) Concave, $f = -15$ cm(II) $x = +40$ cm
(C) Concave, $f = -30$ cm(III) $x = +45$ cm
(D) Convex, $f = +30$ cm(IV) $x = \infty$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
104497.sol:
For the first lens $L_1$ (convex lens at $x = 0$):
Object distance, $u_1 = -30$ cm
Focal length, $f_1 = +20$ cm
Using the lens formula: $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{60} = \dfrac{1}{60}$
$\Rightarrow v_1 = +60$ cm
The image from $L_1$ is formed at $x = +60$ cm.

For the second lens $L_2$ (placed at $x = +30$ cm):
The image formed by $L_1$ acts as a virtual object for $L_2$.
Object distance for $L_2$, $u_2 = +60 - 30 = +30$ cm.

Evaluating each case in List-I:
(A) Convex, $f = +15$ cm:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{15} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3}{30} = \dfrac{1}{10} \Rightarrow v_2 = +10$ cm.
Final coordinate $x = 30 + 10 = +40$ cm. (Matches II)

(B) Concave, $f = -15$ cm:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{-15} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = -\dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{30} \Rightarrow v_2 = -30$ cm.
Final coordinate $x = 30 - 30 = 0$ cm. (Matches I)

(C) Concave, $f = -30$ cm:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{-30} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = -\dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{30} = 0 \Rightarrow v_2 = \infty$.
Final coordinate $x = \infty$. (Matches IV)

(D) Convex, $f = +30$ cm:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{15} \Rightarrow v_2 = +15$ cm.
Final coordinate $x = 30 + 15 = +45$ cm. (Matches III)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

105609.subject: Physics
105609.text:
The work functions of four metals P, Q, R and S are $2.1$ eV, $2.8$ eV, $3.4$ eV and $4.5$ eV respectively. If monochromatic light of wavelength $400$ nm is incident on each of them, which of these metals will exhibit photoelectric emission?
(Take $hc = 1240$ eV nm)
105609.sol:
The energy of an incident photon is given by $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

Substituting the given values:
$E = \dfrac{1240 \text{ eV nm}}{400 \text{ nm}} = 3.1 \text{ eV}$.

For photoelectric emission to occur, the energy of the incident photon must be greater than or equal to the work function of the metal ($E \ge \Phi$).

Comparing the incident photon energy ($E = 3.1 \text{ eV}$) with the given work functions:
For P: $3.1 \text{ eV} > 2.1 \text{ eV}$ (Emission occurs)
For Q: $3.1 \text{ eV} > 2.8 \text{ eV}$ (Emission occurs)
For R: $3.1 \text{ eV} < 3.4 \text{ eV}$ (No emission)
For S: $3.1 \text{ eV} < 4.5 \text{ eV}$ (No emission)

Therefore, only metals P and Q will exhibit photoelectric emission.

Answer: P and Q only

108962.subject: Chemistry
108962.text:
For the equilibrium reaction of the formation of nitric oxide:
$\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}), \Delta \mathrm{H} = +180.7 \text{ kJ}$
Which of the following conditions will favour the maximum yield of $\mathrm{NO}$?
options: High temperature, high pressure and high concentration of $\mathrm{N}_2$
High temperature, high concentration of $\mathrm{O}_2$, and pressure has no effect
Low temperature, high pressure and high concentration of $\mathrm{N}_2$
Low temperature, low pressure and low concentration of $\mathrm{O}_2$
108962.sol:
According to Le Chatelier's principle:

1. The given reaction is endothermic ($\Delta \mathrm{H} > 0$). Endothermic reactions are favoured in the forward direction at high temperatures.

2. The change in the number of gaseous moles is $\Delta \mathrm{n}_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$. Since there is no change in the number of moles of gases, a change in pressure has no effect on the equilibrium position.

3. Increasing the concentration of reactants ($\mathrm{N}_2$ or $\mathrm{O}_2$) shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction to consume the added reactants.

Therefore, high temperature and high concentration of $\mathrm{O}_2$ favour the maximum yield of $\mathrm{NO}$, while pressure has no effect.

113987.text: A solution has a $1: 4$ mole ratio of pentane to hexane. The vapour pressure of the pure hydrocarbons at $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ are 440 mm of Hg for pentane and 120 mm of Hg for hexane. The mole fraction of pentane in the vapour phase would be

$\because$ VP of Pentane in mixture. $=\mathrm{VP}$ of mixture $\times$ mole fraction of pentane in vapour phase
$88=184 \times$ mole fraction of pentane in vapour phase
$\therefore$ Mole fraction of pentane in vapour phase $=\frac{88}{184}=0.478$

117083.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The standard reduction potential $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{M}^{3+}/\mathrm{M}^{2+}}$ for manganese is much more positive than that for iron.

Reason (R): $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ ($d^4$) is easily reduced to the highly stable $d^5$ configuration of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$, whereas $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ already possesses a stable $d^5$ configuration and resists reduction to $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
117083.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: The $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{M}^{3+}/\mathrm{M}^{2+}}$ value for $\mathrm{Mn}$ is highly positive ($+1.57\text{ V}$) compared to that of $\mathrm{Fe}$ ($+0.77\text{ V}$).

Reason (R) is correct and explains (A): A highly positive $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value indicates a strong tendency to get reduced. $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ has a $3d^4$ configuration and readily accepts an electron to form $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$, which has a highly stable exactly half-filled $3d^5$ configuration. On the other hand, $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ already has a stable $3d^5$ configuration, so its reduction to $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ($3d^6$) is thermodynamically less favourable, resulting in a comparatively lower $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

117764.text: Which of the following coordination compounds is capable of exhibiting coordination isomerism?
117764.sol:
Coordination isomerism arises from the interchange of ligands between cationic and anionic entities of different metal ions present in a complex. Therefore, the compound must contain both a complex cation and a complex anion.

Among the given options, only $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4][\mathrm{PdCl}_4]$ consists of a complex cation $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ and a complex anion $[\mathrm{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$. It can exhibit coordination isomerism (for example, forming $[\mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4][\mathrm{PtCl}_4]$).

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{NO}_2)]\mathrm{Cl}_2$ contains an ambidentate ligand and exhibits linkage isomerism.

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_3$ exhibits solvate isomerism.

$\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ contains a simple cation ($\mathrm{K}^+$) and a complex anion, so it cannot show coordination isomerism.

Answer: $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4][\mathrm{PdCl}_4]$

121728.subject: Botany
121728.text: Which of the following is an example of a green alga?
121728.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.Vegetative reproduction usually takes place by fragmentation or by formation of different types of spores. Asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia. The sexual reproduction shows considerable variation in the type and formation of sex cells and it may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. <mark>Some commonly found green algae are: Chlamydomonas</mark>, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra and Chara
121728.meta: Which of the following is an example of a green alga?

121739.subject: Botany
121739.text: What is the shape of the zoospores in brown algae during asexual reproduction?
121739.sol: The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats. They show great variation in size and form. They range from simple branched, filamentous forms (Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a height of 100 meters. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol. The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin. The protoplast contains, in addition to plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus. The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf-like photosynthetic organ – the frond. Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation. <mark>Asexual reproduction in most brown algae is by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped</mark> and have two unequal laterally attached flagella.

121805.subject: Botany
121805.text: How does vegetative reproduction occur in mosses?
options: Through fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema
121805.sol: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of two stages. The first stage is the protonema stage, which develops directly from a spore. It is a creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous stage. The second stage is the leafy stage, which develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. They consist of upright, slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaves. They are attached to the soil through multicellular and branched rhizoids. This stage bears the sex organs. <mark>Vegetative reproduction in mosses is by fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema.</mark> In sexual reproduction, the sex organs antheridia and archegonia are produced at the apex of the leafy shoots. After fertilization, the zygote develops into a sporophyte, consisting of a foot, seta and capsule. The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts. The capsule contains spores. Spores are formed after meiosis. The mosses have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal. Common examples of mosses are Funaria, Polytrichum and Sphagnum

options: both open and closed circulatory system
122219.sol: Annelids have Nephridia which help in osmoregulation and excretion.Annelids possess both longitudinal and circular muscles that help in locomotionAnnelids possess a closed circulatory system. Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral appendages called parapodia, which help in swimming.They may be aquatic (marine and fresh water) or terrestrial; free-living, and sometimes parasitic. 125890.subject: Botany
125890.text: Why is the distribution of some bryophytes and pteridophytes limited?
options: Because of their high pollen production
Due to the need for water for transport of male gametes and fertilisation
Due to their high reliance on insect pollination
125890.sol: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons. As against this, you would recall that water is a regular mode of transport for the male gametes among the lower plant groups such as algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes. It is believed, particularly for some bryophytes and pteridophytes, that their distribution is limited because of the need for water for the transport of male gametes and fertilisation. Some examples of water pollinated plants are Vallisneria and Hydrilla which grow in fresh water and several marine sea-grasses such as Zostera. Not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most of the land plants.

125931.subject: Botany
125931.text: What does the process of bagging involve?
options: Covering flowers with a bag to prevent contamination of stigma with unwanted pollen
Removing leaves from the flower plant
125931.sol: You can easily study pollen germination by dusting some pollen from flowers such as pea, chickpea, Crotalaria, balsam and Vinca on a glass slide containing a drop of sugar solution (about 10 per cent). This is achieved by emasculation and bagging techniques. If the female parent bears bisexual flowers, removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anther dehisces using a pair of forceps is necessary. This step is referred to as emasculation. Emasculated flowers have to be covered with a bag of suitable size, generally made up of butter paper, to prevent contamination of its stigma with unwanted pollen. This process is called bagging. When the stigma of bagged flower attains receptivity, mature pollen grains collected from anthers of the male parent are dusted on the stigma, and the flowers are rebagged, and the fruits allowed to develop

126206.subject: Botany
126206.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The perisperm observed in the mature seeds of black pepper and beet is anatomically distinct from the endosperm.
Reason (R): Perisperm is the persistent remnant of nucellus, whereas endosperm develops from the primary endosperm nucleus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect.
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct.
126206.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct because perisperm and endosperm are two different nutritive tissues found in seeds. Black pepper and beet are classic examples of seeds possessing perisperm.

Reason (R) is also correct and correctly explains the Assertion. Perisperm represents the residual, persistent nucellus (diploid maternal tissue) in the seed. In contrast, endosperm is a newly formed tissue that develops from the triploid primary endosperm nucleus after double fertilization. Because they have entirely different developmental origins, they are anatomically distinct.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

126697.subject: Botany
126697.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the catalytic cycle of an enzyme action.

List-IList-II
A. Substrate bindingI. Breaks chemical bonds of the substrate
B. Induced fitII. Enzyme alters its shape to fit more tightly
C. Active site actionIII. Free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule
D. End of cycleIV. Substrate fits into the active site

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
126697.sol:
According to the catalytic cycle of an enzyme action described in NCERT:

First, the substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme, fitting into the active site (A-IV).

The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate, which is known as induced fit (B-II).

The active site of the enzyme, now in close proximity to the substrate, breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product complex (C-I).

Finally, the enzyme releases the products, and the free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate, marking the end of the cycle (D-III).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

127139.subject: Botany
127139.text: How many plant and animal species have been described so far according to IUCN (2004)?
127139.sol: Since there are published records of all the species discovered and named, we know how many species in all have been recorded so far, but it is not easy to answer the question of how many species there are on earth. According to the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) (2004), the total number of plant and animal species described so far is slightly more than 1.5 million, but we have no clear idea of how many species are yet to be discovered and described. Estimates vary widely and many of them are only educated guesses.

127144.subject: Botany
127144.text: Out of every 10 animals on earth, how many are insects?
127144.sol: More than 70 per cent of all the species recorded are animals, while plants (including algae, fungi, bryophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms) comprise no more than 22 per cent of the total. Among animals, insects are the most species-rich taxonomic group, making up more than 70 per cent of the total. That means, out of every 10 animals on this planet, 7 are insects. Again, how do we explain this enormous diversification of insects? The number of fungi species in the world is more than the combined total of the species of fishes, amphibians, reptiles and mammals

127248.subject: Botany
127248.text: How is India contributing to biodiversity conservation?
127248.sol: Biodiversity conservation may be in situ as well as ex situ. In in situ conservation, the endangered species are protected in their natural habitat so that the entire ecosystem is protected. Recently, 34 ‘biodiversity hotspots’ in the world have been proposed for intensive conservation efforts. Of these, three (Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Himalaya and Indo-Burma) cover India’s rich biodiversity regions. Our country’s in situ conservation efforts are reflected in its 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks, > 450 wildlife sanctuaries and many sacred groves. Ex situ conservation methods include protective maintenance of threatened species in zoological parks and botanical gardens, in vitro fertilisation, tissue culture propagation and cryopreservation of gametes.

127526.subject: Botany
127526.text: Biosphere reserves differ from National Parks and Wildlife sanctuaries because in the former
options: human beings are not allowed to enter
people are an integral part of the system
plants are paid greater attention than the animals
living organisms are brought from all over the world and preserved for posterity.
127526.sol:
Biosphere reserves, National Park and wild life sanctuaries are all protected areas but differ from each other in some ways.
National parks are reserved for betterment of wild life. Cultivation, grazing forestry and habitat manipulations are not allowed.
Sanctuaries are tracts of land with or with out lake where wild life can take refuge without being hunted. Harvesting of timber, collection of forest products, tilling of land, private ownership of land etc., are allowed. Biosphere reserves are multipurpose protected area which are meant for preserving genetic diversity in representative ecosystems of various national biomass and unique biological communities by protecting wild life, traditional life style of tribals and domesticated plant/animal genetic resources.
Each biosphere reserve has 3 zones - (i) core or natural zone - where no human activity is allowed, (ii) Buffer zone - limited human activity is allowed like education and research (iii) Transition zone - It is the outer most zone where an active cooperation is present between reserve management and local people for activities like agriculture, tourism and forestry.
